title: Renewal triage heatmap + QBR segmentation template
content:
Purpose:
A compact, operational heatmap + segmentation sheet to use during quarterly business reviews and renewal triage. Goal is to help CSMs and AMs rapidly prioritize outreach, enable playbook selection, and feed renewal risk signals back into product/ops.

How to use (quick):
- Populate one row per customer account (or per contract if multiple).
- Columns capture taxonomy + signals: tier, ICP-fit, deployment mode, region, ARR, active seats, weekly usage, top-3 usage flows, infra footprint (hosted/dedicated/private), recent incidents, NPS (last 90d), support cases (30/90d), product regressions, contract renewal date, stakeholder health.
- Score each customer on two axis: Renewal Risk (0-10) and Strategic Importance (0-10).
- Heatmap quadrant determines recommended playbook/actions.
- Feed high-risk strategic accounts to AE/solutions-engineering for immediate engagement.

Suggested columns (sheet-friendly):
- Account Name
- Redwood Account ID / Sales ACCT
- Tier (1 / 2 / 3)
- ICP-Fit Score (0-10) -- rubric below
- Deployment Mode (hosted | dedicated | private)
- Region (NA | EMEA | APAC)
- ARR (USD)
- ARR Trend (↑ / → / ↓)
- Weekly Active Tokens / avg latency (line)
- Key Product Use Cases (short list)
- Infra Footprint Notes (GPU type, quantization, cache usage)
- NPS (last survey)
- Support Cases: last 30d / 90d
- Recent Sev Incidents (Y/N + short note)
- Time to first response (SRE/Support SLA)
- Contract Renewal Date
- Renewal Owner (CSM / AE)
- Renewal Risk Score (0-10) -- compute guidance below
- Strategic Importance Score (0-10)
- Heatmap Quadrant (auto from scores)
- Recommended Playbook (see playbook mapping)
- Action Items (owner|ETA|status)
- Notes / Link to QBR deck

Scoring rubrics (short):
- ICP-Fit (0-10): 10=core use case aligns with Redwood strengths (low-latency, high-throughput), heavy token volumes, product roadmap aligned; 0=rare use, eval-only.
- Renewal Risk (0-10): composite of ARR trend, support/incidents, engagement, exec sponsor health. Suggested weights: ARR trend (20%), incidents/support (30%), usage drop (25%), exec sponsor (25%).
- Strategic Importance (0-10): revenue + reference potential + partner sync + legal/compliance strategic value.

Heatmap quadrant -> quick playbook mapping (starter):
- High Strategic / High Risk (red-hot): AE + CSM + Solutions-eng rescue. Immediate exec outreach, rollback options, usage pulse checks, canary to fallback models, PST (product success timeboxed) + weekly exec sync.
- High Strategic / Low Risk (strategic-green): Proactive expansion motion; map expansion plays, propose dedicated capacity discounts, roadmap sync. Standard QBR cadence + SLAs review.
- Low Strategic / High Risk (low-revenue risk): Triage low-touch remediation: support escalations, technical healthcheck, self-serve enablement, offer office hours with Solutions Eng. Consider churn containment credit vs cost.
- Low Strategic / Low Risk (monitor): Keep standard nurture, automated health nudges, add to monthly low-touch QBRs.

Example quick formulas (for sheet):
- Heatmap quadrant = if(Risk>=7 && Strategic>=7, "HH", if(Risk>=7, "LH", if(Strategic>=7, "HL", "LL")))  -- mapping HH=HighStrategicHighRisk, etc.
- Renewal Risk composite example: =ROUND( (0.2*ARR_trend_score + 0.3*Incidents_score + 0.25*Usage_change_score + 0.25*Exec_sponsor_score), 0)

Playbook snippets (copy-paste for action items):
- "Rescue + Exec": schedule CSM+AE+SE deep-dive within 48h, collect top 5 blocked flows, attach perf trace, propose 2 immediate mitigations (fallback model, increase cache TTL). Owner: AE / ETA: 2 business days.
- "Expansion Pack": present dedicated pricing path + 3-month pilot; run ROI calc for token unit economics. Owner: CSM + Product Ops.
- "Low-touch remediation": open support playbook ticket, schedule 2-hour healthcheck, send triage checklist, monitor for 14 days.

Signals / thresholds we use in practice (notes):
- Usage drop > 30% MoM for 2 consecutive weeks = risk trigger.
- 2+ sev incidents in 30d = risk trigger.
- Exec sponsor change (named PO leaves) = +2 risk points.
- Dedicated/private customers have higher operational risk weight (incidents matter more).

QBR prep checklist for CSMs (short):
- Update sheet row + attach last 3 weeks usage graph (GA/Prometheus).
- Confirm exec list + renewal date in Salesforce.
- Link QBR deck + list of open action items.
- If HH quadrant, escalate to AE + Solutions Eng 72h prior.

Sample row (text example):
- Acme Robotics | RW-01234 | Tier 1 | ICP-Fit 9 | private | NA | $1,200,000 | ↑ | tokens 12M/wk, p50 110ms | real-time assist, summarization | GPU: A100x2, kv-cache | NPS 52 | 1/3 cases (30/90d) | 1 sev last 21d | SLA RT 2h | renewal 2026-07-01 | CSM: Zara Chen | Risk 8 | Strategic 9 | HH | Playbook: Rescue + Exec | Actions: AE sync (Lucas) 2026-03-15 pending

Notes to self / open questions (working):
- Need a standard canonical mapping from "deployment mode" to our operational weight table (who owns incidents for private customers?).
- Should we bias Strategic score for customers in regulated industries (healthcare, finance)? current plan: +1 bump if regulated. Need exec sign-off.
- How to incorporate Redwood Optimize suggestions (quant/kv-cache) as a proactive expansion item in the sheet? Consider dedicated column: "Optimization suggestions applied" Y/N.
- Link to audit: Jira ticket for private-deploy playbook: JIRA-CSUP-487 (see linked artifacts).
